chunks: Saad narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Ali al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no (zakat) in what is less than five awsaq, and the wasq is sixty sa's.

key_terms.أَوْسَاقٍ: plural of wasq, a unit of volume/weight for grains
key_terms.الْوَسْقُ: a specific unit of measurement, defined here as sixty sa's
key_terms.شَيْءٌ: nothing, indicating the absence of obligation below the threshold
key_terms.صَاعًا: a traditional unit of volume used for measuring zakat

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of grain subject to zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* explicitly defines the nisab for zakat on staple grains and fruits, establishing five awsaq (300 sa's) as the minimum taxable threshold. By linking the measurement to the Prophet’s household, it underscores the precision of Shia juristic calculations regarding agricultural wealth, distinguishing it from other asset classes.
